page: OVHcloud c2-60-flex is a compute-oriented virtual server provisioned on KVM hypervisor architecture. It features 16 dedicated physical cores powered by an x86_64 Intel Haswell processor running at 3.0 GHz with single-thread-per-core allocation. System memory is configured at 60 GB, equating to 3.75 GB of RAM per core. The instance includes 50 GB of local SSD storage and a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps. It does not include dedicated graphics hardware, and public IPv4 addresses are not provisioned complimentary by default. Processor flags support AVX, AES, and FMA, but do not support AVX-512 or AMX extensions.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier compute and memory metrics across standard testing suites. In CPU benchmarks, the instance recorded a stress-ng multi-core score of 24,265.94, a PassMark CPU score of 23,991.37, and a Geekbench multi-core score of 9,335.0. Uncached large-block memory bandwidth reached 127.34 GB/sec for reads and 44.15 GB/sec for writes. Database and web throughput tests recorded 23.34 million operations per second for Redis SET tasks and 18.32 GB/sec for static web serving. Conversely, execution in language model generation tested weak, achieving 44.37 tokens per second on a 135M model and 7.45 tokens per second on a 7B model.

The 1:1 physical core assignment provides deterministic execution by eliminating hyper-threading thread contention. Cost efficiency reflects a balance between multi-core processing density and overall resource footprint. Tradeoffs include the relatively modest 50 GB local storage capacity and baseline 1 Gbps network interface, which limit high-throughput data ingress or expansive on-disk storage requirements. The configuration fits software compilation, CI/CD build environments, batch processing, and caching services where processing consistency is required over expansive local disk volume.
description: OVHcloud c2-60-flex is a compute-focused instance delivering 16 dedicated physical x86_64 Intel Haswell cores running at 3.0 GHz without hyper-threading. The instance features 60 GB of RAM (3.75 GB per core), 50 GB of local SSD storage, and a 1 Gbps baseline network throughput. Discrete graphics processors are not included. Benchmark results place the server within mid-tier categories for multi-core compute and memory bandwidth, posting a PassMark CPU score of 23,991.37 and handling 23.34 million Redis SET operations per second. However, generative LLM text processing speeds fall into lower performance brackets due to hardware age and lack of advanced vector extensions. Tradeoffs center on the constrained 50 GB local disk capacity and basic network ceiling. The instance is suited for multi-threaded build jobs, batch execution, web services, and caching workloads.
